answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a bonded escrow, not identity papers. An agent must lock capital that acts as an anchor for its stake, and that stake unlocks only after a long unbonding delay. Spinning up many puppet identities means posting many full stakes, so cost grows linearly with the number of fake agents while per-agent reward stays flat. Proven collusion slashes the stake, making the attack a net loss. Reputation adds a second filter: attestations are weighted by operator track record, a slow river fed by verified work, so freshly funded ivory identities start with near-zero weight.
